content.text: The text surveys liver and biliary diseases. Hepatic abscess may be fatal, especially when multiple or pyaemic, but early aspiration and drainage improve survival. It differentiates abscess from hydatids, cancer, empyema, and gallbladder disease. Acute yellow atrophy and phosphorus poisoning cause jaundice, hepatic cell destruction, hemorrhage, and coma. Liver cancer produces painful nodular enlargement, wasting, ascites, and is incurable; amyloid and fatty liver cause slower, usually smooth enlargement associated with chronic suppuration, cachexia, obesity, or alcoholism. Bile-duct catarrh, gallstones, and obstruction produce jaundice, colic, digestive disturbance, and potentially cirrhosis or death. Portal thrombosis and suppurative pylephlebitis cause ascites, fever, hemorrhage, and hepatic abscesses. Hydatid cysts are slow-growing and treated mainly by aspiration or surgery. Pancreatic disease causes maldigestion, fatty stools, wasting, pain, jaundice, and sometimes diabetes. John journeyed to the bedroom.
